mechanism_narrative: A three-week rise in RETAIL_REC from -42.9 to -38.6 creates persistent momentum that lifts the next 28-day mean above the last 28-day mean.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC increased from -42.9 at t-3w to -38.6 at t-0w
failure_condition: The next 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is less than or equal to the last 28-day mean despite RETAIL_REC rising for three consecutive weekly means.

mechanism_narrative: A TRANSIT crossing above -40 after two weeks below -40 signals restored public-transit trip-making, which raises RETAIL_REC over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT weekly mean crosses above -40 after two consecutive weeks below -40
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose from -42.7 at t-2w to -37.7 at t-0w
failure_condition: Following a TRANSIT crossing above -40, the next 14-day mean of RETAIL_REC is not higher than the prior 14-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Joint weekly increases in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT signal a broad return of commuting and out-of-home routines, which amplifies retail footfall and raises RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both increase week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -31.0 at t-2w to -24.4 at t-0w and TRANSIT rose from -42.7 to -37.7
failure_condition: When WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both rise week-on-week, RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days is lower than over the prior 14 days.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM near baseline at -0.4% indicates that essential shopping no longer absorbs precautionary trips, so consumers shift time to retail and recreation, raising RETAIL_REC over the next week.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved from -4.3 at t-3w to -0.4 at t-0w
failure_condition: When GROCERY_PHARM is within 1 point of baseline, RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days is not higher than over the prior 7 days.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility recovering from -26.0 to -15.4 reflects a seasonal shift to outdoor activity that spills over into retail and recreation spending, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved from -26.0 at t-3w to -15.4 at t-0w
failure_condition: If PARKS continues to recover but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days, the seasonal spillover mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility from 25.7 to 22.6 shows people are leaving home more; a further drop below 22.0 releases additional out-of-home consumption that raises RETAIL_REC over the next week.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined from 25.7 at t-2w to 22.6 at t-0w
failure_condition: When RESIDENTIAL falls below 22.0, RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days is not higher than over the prior 7 days.

mechanism_narrative: In a tightening-restrictions regime, WORKPLACES below -20 and TRANSIT below -35 suppress commuter and leisure travel capacity, so retail demand stalls and RETAIL_REC falls over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES at -24.4 and TRANSIT at -37.7 at t-0w
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES < -20 and TRANSIT < -35, RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: In a reopening regime with falling RESIDENTIAL mobility, TRANSIT recovery amplifies retail footfall; joint TRANSIT and RESIDENTIAL signals raise RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL declines week-on-week while TRANSIT rises week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose from -42.7 to -37.7 and RESIDENTIAL fell from 25.7 to 22.6 between t-2w and t-0w
failure_condition: In a reopening regime, when RESIDENTIAL declines week-on-week while TRANSIT rises week-on-week, RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not higher than over the last 28 days.
